chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ja'far ibn Isa, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! A woman dies, and her father claims that he had lent her some of the possessions and servants that were with her. Is his claim accepted without proof, or is his claim not accepted except with proof?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'It is permissible without proof.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And I wrote to him that if the husband of the deceased woman, or her father-in-law, or her mother-in-law, were to claim regarding her possessions or her servants, similar to what her father had claimed regarding the loan of some of the possessions or the servants, would they be in the same status as the father in the claim?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'No.'
ai.seo_question: Can a father claim lent items from his deceased daughter's estate without proof?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'bi-la bayyinah' (acceptance without proof) in inheritance disputes, specifically granting the deceased woman's father a privileged status to claim lent items or servants from her estate without requiring evidence. In contrast, the husband or his parents are not accorded this same presumption, highlighting a nuanced distinction in Shia jurisprudence regarding familial hierarchy and evidentiary burdens in estate settlement.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ja’far Al Kufy, from Muhammad Bin Al Ismail, from Ja’far Bin Isa who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The woman dies, so her father claims that he had lent to her what was with her, from the possessions, and a servant. Would his testimony be accepted for his claim without a proof, or his claim would not be acceptable except with the proof?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to him: ‘It is allowed without proof’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And I wrote to him<sup>asws</sup> that if a husband of the deceased woman were to claim, or father of her husband, or mother of her husband, with regards to possessions, or regarding a servant, similar to what her father had claimed from having lent some of the possessions, or the servant. Would they be with regards to that, at the status of the father?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Yazid ibn Ishaq from Harun ibn Hamzah who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of one who hires a man who because of not being able to trust each other, places the wages in the hand of another man who dies without any replacement and the wages vanish.

He (the Imam) said, ‘The person hiring is responsible for the wages of the worker until he pays, unless the worker has told him to do so and agreed to give it to that person; if so then his right is where he agreed to be placed.’”
